title: Incident announce bar and handoff snippet cards
creator: Ethan Reyes
description:
Problem: Engineers and on-call responders report that when an alert escalates during high-traffic windows it's difficult for product stakeholders and secondary responders to quickly understand scope, expected cost impact, and who to hand off to. Existing incident entry surfaces are full-page and noisy; we need a lightweight, ephemeral surface that announces an incident and provides actionable handoff snippets without forcing a full context switch.

Goal: Design an 'Incident Announce Bar' (IAB) — a compact, persistent banner anchored to the top of the Console workspace for the first 30 minutes after an alert is opened — plus a set of 'Handoff Snippet Cards' that surface key metadata (primary on-call, backup, runbook link, quick postmortem link, rough cost delta estimate) and quick actions (message on Slack, escalate, pin to incident). The surface should: be low-distraction, show SLO delta at-a-glance, surface a tiny cost delta with confidence band, and allow one-click handoff.

Key user scenarios: 1) Primary responder acknowledges and needs to pass on to a second shift: they click 'Create Handoff Snippet' which prepopulates contact and notes; second responder receives a compact card in their Console view. 2) Product manager wants to know potential cost exposure: they glance at the cost delta chip on the bar (green/amber/red) and click for a small modal with cost breakdown. 3) Incidents that have been open >3 hours will show a 'link-to-postmortem' affordance that auto-populates the PM's draft postmortem doc.

Acceptance criteria: 1) IAB prototype implemented in Figma with responsive states (desktop 1366+, narrow 760-1024, collapsed mobile). 2) Handoff Snippet Card pattern with fields: title, summary, primary, backup, runbook link, cost-delta, SLO-impact snapshot, QuickActions (Slack, PagerDuty, Pin, Create Postmortem). 3) Design tokens and spacing consistent with Console styles; accessible color contrast >=4.5:1 for critical chips. 4) Usability checklist: 3 user tests with on-call engineers and PMs show successful handoff in <90s. 5) Handoff payload spec documented and linked to ENG-19821.

Deliverables: 1) High-fidelity Figma prototype (IAB + 3 handoff flows). 2) Clickable micro-interaction specs (dismiss, snooze, expand card, copy-to-clipboard for handoff snippet). 3) Confluence PRD with acceptance criteria, API payload example, and rollout notes. 4) Accessibility pass and QA checklist.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Marisol: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focused on anchoring behavior and small-screen collapse. Flagged question about whether the announce bar should be user-dismissable or time-bound by default.

2026-02-12 - Ethan: Research notes from on-call interviews (n=6) attached. Findings: responders prefer prepopulated handoff text and explicit 'handoff accepted' acknowledgements; cost chip should be optional per project settings.

2026-02-13 - PM Samir Gupta: Suggested adding a 'confidence' tooltip for the cost estimate and linking to the billing dashboard. Also want guardrails for P0 incidents to auto-pin the snippet to the incident timeline.

2026-02-14 - Design critique: Team feedback (Anna, Keiko, Jonas) - prefer iconography for SLO delta vs text, reduce text density in card summary, ensure 24px tap targets for quick actions. Action: Marisol to iterate microcopy and spacing.

2026-02-16 - Marisol: Updated high-fidelity with color states (cost green/amber/red), added keyboard shortcut to open the handoff composer (Shift+H), and prototype for 'snooze 15/60 mins' behavior. Pushed changes and asked ENG for API field mapping.

2026-02-17 - Eng feedback (from ENG-19821 thread): payload OK but rename 'cost_estimate' -> 'cost_delta_est_usd' and include 'cost_confidence_pct'. ENG requested explicit schema examples. Adding to PRD.
2026-02-18 - Usability test planning: scheduled 3 remote sessions with on-call rota group; test script uploaded. After tests we'll incorporate adjustments and hand off to frontend for spike.
design_notes: Iteration 1: top-anchored persistent banner with collapse arrow. Included SLO sparkline but testers found it noisy.
Iteration 2: replaced sparkline with SLO delta chip + hover for trend; moved sparkline into expanded card to reduce visual noise.
Decision: cost delta will be an opt-in project-level toggle. For orgs with cost-sensitivity enabled, default show; otherwise hidden behind 'Show cost' control on the announce bar.
Accessibility: ensured focus trap on expanded card, and all quick actions reachable via keyboard. Color tokens use semantic tokens: token-alert-critical, token-alert-warning, token-alert-ok.
reviews: 2026-02-15 - PM review (Samir): 'Strong direction; ensure postmortem flow links to existing templates and that non-admins cannot auto-create docs.'
2026-02-16 - SRE review (Priya): 'Cost estimate useful but needs guardrails; suggest limiting visibility for incidents created by infra ops.'
2026-02-17 - Security review kickoff: outreach to SecOps to confirm no sensitive metadata is surfaced in the public announce bar.
next_steps: Finish usability testing and incorporate feedback (due 2026-02-20)
Finalize PRD with payload schema and handoff acceptance events (E2E)
Create frontend spike ticket for IAB prototype and link to ENG-19821
Coordinate rollout flag with product to gate cost visibility per-project
notes_for_engineering: Payload example added to PRD: { title, summary, primary_oncall, backup_oncall, runbook_url, cost_delta_est_usd, cost_confidence_pct, slo_delta_pct, created_by, created_at }
Frontend should implement compact CSS variables to allow embedding within Console header; mobile collapse should convert to a 44px tall pill with expand chevron.
Telemetry events: announce_bar_shown, handoff_created, handoff_accepted, cost_detail_clicked, announce_bar_dismissed.
